concepts.def: Assume the hypotheses; deduce the conclusion by valid steps. Most common form for identities and divisibility.
Assume the negation; derive a contradiction; conclude original statement. Classic: irrationality of √2.
Disprove a universal claim by exhibiting a single case where it fails. One counterexample suffices.
Base case + inductive step (assume true for n = k, prove for n = k + 1). Used for sums, divisibility, inequalities.
Many proofs (identities, inequalities) reduce to careful algebra: factorisation, completing the square, AM-GM.
If P then Q is not the same as if Q then P. Be careful with converses; quantifiers (∀, ∃) change meaning.
